Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key clinical findings  
• 23-year-old female with 3-day history of constant, worsening lower abdominal pain (8/10) centered below umbilicus, associated with light vaginal bleeding post-menses, recent nausea, and constipation (resolved). No fever, dysuria, shoulder pain, or syncope.  

Working diagnosis  
• Pelvic pain—rule out ectopic pregnancy (high priority given reproductive age, pain, bleeding, and last pregnancy test 1 month ago despite contraceptive implant).  

Differential considerations (consistent with DDx)  
• Pelvic inflammatory disease (medium likelihood) – pelvic pain, bleeding, discharge, sexually active, but afebrile and no exam findings yet.  
• Ovarian torsion or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst (medium likelihood) – severe constant pain, light bleeding possible; localization not clearly unilateral.  

Plan  
• Arrange urgent face-to-face abdominal and pelvic examination.  
• Patient to perform home pregnancy test today; if positive, instructed to call immediately for urgent review.  
• If pain worsens or unable to tolerate oral intake, advised to seek urgent care.  
• Support line contact provided to book in-person appointment.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Ectopic pregnancy – High likelihood: Reproductive-age woman with lower abdominal pain and light post-menses bleeding; implant failure possible; urgent to exclude.  
2. Pelvic inflammatory disease – Medium likelihood: Bilateral pelvic pain with bleeding and discharge in sexually active patient; afebrile but exam pending.  
3. Ovarian torsion / hemorrhagic ovarian cyst – Medium likelihood: Severe constant pelvic pain with possible light bleeding; needs imaging/exam for confirmation.
